title: Simultaneous Epp base change for finitely many traits
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $W_0$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ with perfect residue field $k_0$ and fraction field $K_0$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-field]. Mixed characteristic means characteristic zero for the fraction field and characteristic $p$ for the residue field; perfect means that Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective. Let $I$ be a finite set. For each $i\in I$ let $T_i$ be an excellent discrete valuation ring with an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow T_i$ [def-exc-excellent-ring], fraction field $F_i$, and residue field $\kappa_i$. Local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal. Assume that every element of $\bigcap_{n\geq0}\kappa_i^{p^n}$ is algebraic over the induced copy of $k_0$, where $\kappa_i^{p^n}=\{x^{p^n}:x\in\kappa_i\}$. Then there is an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow W$ making $W$ a finite $W_0$-module, where $W$ is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ whose residue field is a finite extension of $k_0$, hence perfect [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-pc-field-extension]. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(W)$ and let $\pi$ be any uniformizer of $W$. For each $i$, take any field factor $E$ of $F_i\otimes_{K_0}K$; the tensor product is a finite product of fields, and field factor means a quotient by a maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $B_{i,E}\subset E$ be the integral closure of the image of $T_i\otimes_{W_0}W$ in $E$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $B_{i,E}/\pi B_{i,E}$ is reduced: it has no nonzero nilpotent elements. The rings $T_i$ need not be complete, and $I$ may be empty.

source.place: Expose IV Theorem 3.1.2, Remark 3.1.3 (noncomplete upper trait), and 4.2.3, sentence beginning De tels ideaux p etant en nombre fini: simultaneous finite base change, using stability under further finite base change.

proof.text: For each $i\in I$, the hypotheses of [lem-per-epp-single-trait-base-change] hold for $T=T_i$: $W_0$ is the given complete mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field, the map $W_0\hookrightarrow T_i$ is injective and local, $T_i$ is excellent, and the perfect-core algebraicity assumption is exactly the displayed hypothesis on $\kappa_i$. Clause (1) of that theorem gives a finite extension $W_i'$ of $W_0$ (a complete discrete valuation ring, finite over $W_0$ through an injective local map) which is good for $T_i$: every field factor $E$ of $F_i\otimes_{K_0}\operatorname{Frac}(W_i')$ has normalized image of $T_i\otimes_{W_0}W_i'$ with reduced fibre modulo a uniformizer of $W_i'$.

Because $I$ is finite, [lem-per-epp-common-finite-trait-extension] supplies one complete discrete valuation ring $W$ finite over $W_0$ and local maps $W_i'\hookrightarrow W$ for all $i$. Its residue field is a finite extension of the perfect field $k_0$, hence perfect. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $W$ and put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(W)$.

source.place: Expose IV §4.2.3, finite family and finite common base change

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, take $W=W_0$; it is finite over itself through the identity, complete, mixed characteristic with perfect residue field, and the conclusion is vacuous. Otherwise let $W$ be as in Step 2. It is a finite extension of $W_0$ in the sense of [lem-per-epp-single-trait-base-change], and Step 2 gives a local $W_0$-algebra map $W_i'\to W$ for each $i$. Since $W_i'$ is good for $T_i$, clause (3) of that theorem shows that $W$ is good for $T_i$. Unwinding the definition with $W'=W$, $K'=K$ and the uniformizer $\pi$: for every field factor $E$ of $F_i\otimes_{K_0}K$, the integral closure $B_{i,E}$ in $E$ of the image of $T_i\otimes_{W_0}W$ satisfies that $B_{i,E}/\pi B_{i,E}$ is reduced. This holds for every $i$ and every $E$, proving the assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q128-c4ecc0c57 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read ILO IV Thm 3.1.2 (Epp), Rem 3.1.3 (mixed-characteristic reducedness; only S needs to be complete) and the §4.2.3 sentence 'De tels idéaux p étant en nombre fini … stable par changement de base fini'. The item statement matches the finite-family use in §4.2.3: injective local = local dominant, T_i excellent (automatic for a DVR with characteristic-0 fraction field), the empty family allowed, and the conclusion independent of the uniformizer. The citer lem-per-mixed-reduced-special-fibre-cover (steps 3 and 7) uses it consistently. The split mirrors the source: the one-trait Epp theorem (the theorem ILO cites), then a common finite extension, then stability. It is not a relabelling. Both new nodes are true. Stability, checked by hand: each localization of B_E is a DVR with uniformizer π', and its residue field is separable over the perfect field k'. So (D⊗W'')/π'' = κ_D⊗_{k'}k'' is reduced and B'⊗W'' is already the normalization of T⊗W''. Common extension: take W = integral closure of W_0 in a compositum; it is finite (Nagata) and a complete DVR (unique extension of the valuation), each W_i is the integral closure of W_0 in its fraction field so W_i ⊂ W, and the residue field is finite and perfect. Duplicate search: grep of the DAG for Epp, elimination of ramification, reduced special fibre and compositum found only different facts (perfect-core nodes, trf valuation reducedness, sbc tame nodes, lem-weil-common-extension-fields); the blueprint has no Epp node. No SGA, no off-unit citations. One fault, repaired (B2/E6): the single-trait node stated stability as 'the corresponding normalized integral closures after base change to W''', which is vague and did not require a W_0-compatible local map W'→W''; it also said 'Let p>0' and left terms undefined. Rewrote it with 'finite extension', 'field factor', B_E and 'good for T' defined inline, as clauses (1) existence, (2) T⊗W' reduced, (3) stability along local W_0-maps, and added def-weil-finitely-generated-module to stmt_deps.
